To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. We find that the O(g2a)-matching coefficients for all operators of interest have the same sign.

the one-loop matching coefficients for the lattice operators relevant to $ {B^ 0} - {\overline{B}^ 0} $ mixing and B-meson decaying are non-zero for domain-wall light quars and O(a)-improved heavy quarks.
We have computed the O(g2a)-order perturbative matching of the lattice operators for the B-meson matrix elements and $ {B} - {\bar {B}} $ mixing with static quarks and domain wall fermions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perturbative matching of static-light operators in the static-light quark system.
the perturbative matching of the lattice operators relevant to heavy-light meson decays and mixing.
the matching of lattice operators to continuum operators at one loop in perturbation theory, with the aim of providing a framework to calculate physical quantities from lattice simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the O(g2a)/O(g0) matching of the lattice operators to the continuum operators for the static-light system with O(a)/O(a2) improved light and heavy quarks is now under control.

the static heavy quark and domain-wall light-quark system is a very promising approach to the study of $ {B^+} \to D_s^ + \gamma $, $ {B_s} \to J/\psi \phi $, and $ {B_s}(s\bar s) - {\bar{K}}(s\bar d) $ mixing.
the O(a) improvement of the static heavy-light operators in the static heavy-light system is a must for the precision lattice QCD study of the CKM physics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the O(g2a)-matching coefficients of all operators are well under control, and the matching coefficients of the operators relevant to B-decays and $ { B^0} - \bar B^0$ mixing are small and can be reliably computed.
the O(g2a), O(a) and O(a2) matching factors are available for all the operators of interest in this paper.
the O(a) corrections are large and positive, and the HYP2 static quark action is the best of the three static quark actions that we studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the static-light OPE is a powerful tool for extracting the physical matrix elements of the operators of interest from lattice simulations.
the O(g2a)-improved static-light operators are not renormalized by O(a) effects and that the O(g3a) corrections to the matching coefficients are negligible.
O(a) matching can be done reliably with a small set of operators and a few simulations with a variety of lattice actions.
